ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, power supply E is located below, with one node at each of its two ends; voltmeter V is connected between these two power-supply terminal nodes, so it measures the terminal voltage of the power supply. On the upper part of the outer loop there are resistor R and switch S; resistor R and switch S are connected in series; when S is closed, the outer branch forms a closed loop, and R is connected across the terminal voltage of the power supply. Reasoning: The problem gives R = 58 Ω. When the switch is closed, the voltmeter reading is 5.8 V, which is the terminal voltage applied across the external resistor R. The resistance of an ideal switch can be ignored, so when closed, the circuit current I = V/R = 5.8/58 = 0.10 A.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the voltmeter is across the source, and R is the external load switched into the circuit. From the text, use the open-switch voltmeter reading to set E = 6.0 V. Use the closed-switch terminal voltage V = 5.8 V and R = 58 ohm. Infer internal resistance from V/E = R/(R+r): r = 58(6.0/5.8 - 1) = 2 ohm. Then compute the closed-circuit current from I = E/(R+r) = 6.0/(58+2) = 0.10 A.
method.CoT_raw: Image description: The diagram shows a cell/source labeled E at the bottom. A voltmeter V is connected across the two terminals of the source, so it measures the terminal voltage of the source. The external circuit branch contains a resistor R in series with a switch S, so when S is closed the resistor is connected as the load. Reasoning: With S open, no load current flows, so the voltmeter reads the emf: E = 6.0 V. With S closed, the terminal voltage is 5.8 V across the external load R = 58 Ω. Using the source model with internal resistance r, V/E = R/(R + r). Thus r = 58(6.0/5.8 - 1) = 2 Ω. The closed-circuit current is I = E/(R + r) = 6.0/(58 + 2) = 0.10 A.
